title: Introduce per-service geozone fences and KMS accountability adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds per-service geozone enforcement middleware and a KMS accountability adapter. Backwards-compatible config flags added; enabled by default for new tenants. See rollout notes for canary and migration steps.
description: Context: Customers with strict data residency requirements asked for finer-grained enforcement at the service level instead of the current global/tenant pinning. This PR adds a per-service geozone fence that evaluates runtime request claims and operator scopes, and pairs it with a KMS accountability adapter that emits immutable provenance assertions into the audit pipeline. Motivation: make region-pin decisions auditable and enforceable for mixed-tenant workloads where a single tenant may operate services with different residency constraints. Changes are designed to be incremental and reversible via feature flags. Summary of changes: - New geozone_fence middleware (service-level) that consults: service manifest annotations, operator-scoped claims, and a residency policy cache. - KMS accountability adapter: decorates KMS calls with a signed lightweight proof (prov_header) that is recorded by the audit forwarder; proof includes service id, operator id, and claimed region (packed and HMACed). - Migration shim: a short-running upgrade job that backfills service residency annotations for legacy manifests based on policy heuristics and admin overrides. - Config: feature flags under flags.security.geozone_fence and flags.security.kms_accountability; rollout strategy documented in console release notes. - Tests: unit coverage for policy evaluation, integration test that simulates cross-zone operator attempts and verifies audit proof emission and rejection paths. - Observability: new metrics (geozone.allow/deny, kms.proof.emitted, kms.proof.rejected) and a dashboard JSON with example queries. Rollout plan (high level): 1) Deploy middleware off by default; run migration job to populate annotations. 2) Enable geozone_fence in canary region for monitoring (3 days). 3) Enable KMS accountability adapter in canary and verify audit chain. 4) Gradual ramp and post-deploy audit consistency check. Security considerations: keys used by the adapter are short-lived signing keys derived from the platform KMS; adapter falls back to a deterministic non-signed marker when signing is unavailable and records an elevated audit tag for follow-up. Ops runbook: abort/disable flags and a clear audit query to find affected requests are provided in the runbook. Backwards compatibility: policy defaults keep previous tenant-level behaviour when service annotations are missing. Motivation and design rationale are discussed in the linked Linear ticket. This description includes the checklist and implementation notes below.

review_discussion: Arjun Patel: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) make the HMAC fallback explicit in the audit logs, (2) ensure the migration shim can be re-run idempotently.
Maya Chen: Addressed both — HMAC fallback now emits a kms.proof.fallback metric and migration job is idempotent and locks per-service during backfill.
Stefan Müller: Can we ensure the adapter doesn't add >200 bytes to the audit record? Concern about storage growth.
Maya Chen: Prov_header compacted and base64 encoded; typical extra size ~128 bytes. Added retention guidance to docs.
Lin Wei: Integration test passed in staging, verified that a cross-region operator was rejected and the audit proof recorded the attempted region (for follow-up). Approving.
Arjun Patel: LGTM, merging after CI green.

notes_for_prod: If increased audit storage is observed, temporarily disable kms_accountability adapter via flags.security.kms_accountability=false and run the audit consistency report. For unexpected denials, use the admin override endpoint described in the runbook to accept and then open a support ticket.
